The same-language comparator resolves the earlier section hold; this decision is not automatically extended to neighbouring languages.

These bare uṭh responses are imperatives/stems of “get up”, not the past participle *ut-sthita (1907). Responses containing negative particles, auxiliaries or perfect endings are excluded from this rule.

Turner explicitly gives Marathi āī “mother” in the *āī nursery-word family. Survey āy represents the same final glide; the meaning is exact. No claim about an Indo-European root or the competing Dardic āryikā analysis is made for this Marathi form.
